changelog.title: Softcap — what's new
changelog.v0118_li1: Softcap no longer reads the Codex CLI's files. An account is added through the browser and read live from the service with a grant of its own, so there is no snapshot age left to explain.
changelog.v0118_li2: The cost: usage updates on the poll rather than the instant Codex writes a line, and an account that was only ever picked up from the CLI needs one browser sign-in.
changelog.v0118_li3: An empty window now says which kind of empty it is — still looking on a fresh install, rather than concluding that nothing is there.
changelog.v0118_p: Codex accounts now come from the browser, and only from there:
changelog.v0121_li1: The Claude Code keychain item is no longer opened. Every account — Claude and Codex alike — is added through the browser and holds a grant of its own, so nothing here asks macOS for permission to read another app's data.
changelog.v0121_li2: That removes the prompts that came with it: no keychain password when you press Refresh, no “Allow access…”, and no window telling you credentials cannot be read.
changelog.v0121_li3: The cost: an account that used to appear by itself because you had run claude /login needs one browser sign-in. A token copied from the CLI by an older build is never spent — that would rotate it and sign the CLI out — so those rows ask to be signed in once.
changelog.v0121_p: Softcap now reads nothing but its own credentials:
changelog.v012_li1: Several Claude and Codex accounts at once, added through the browser or detected from a local CLI.
changelog.v012_li2: A menu bar timer — countdown, percentage, both or just the icon — and a shortcut of your choosing to open the window.
changelog.v012_li3: Widgets in all four sizes on macOS; home and lock screen on iPhone.
changelog.v012_li4: Threshold notifications at 80% and 95%, or your own levels, with quiet hours.
changelog.v012_li5: Ten interface languages, including Arabic laid out right to left.
changelog.v012_li6: Credentials in the keychain only; error reports and the update check both optional, both scrubbed-or-off.
changelog.v012_note: Builds are signed ad-hoc for now, so the first launch takes a right-click and an Open — the support page shows both ways through.
changelog.v012_p: The first public build. Everything the landing page describes, shipping:
faq.a1: For every account you add it shows the two windows a subscription runs on: the five-hour session limit and the weekly limit — what is used, what is left, and when each resets.
faq.a10: The app is free. On the wire it costs one usage request per account per poll — every five minutes in the background, once a minute with the window open, or whatever interval you set.
faq.a2: No. Softcap reads usage endpoints with your own credentials; the requests carry no prompt and run no model, so the quota they describe is not touched by describing it.
faq.a3: Claude and OpenAI Codex, several accounts of each at once. Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and the GLM Coding Plan are not supported yet: a provider that cannot be checked against a live account would quietly show zero, which is worse than nothing.
faq.a4: Signing in through the browser with OAuth gives Softcap a grant of its own. The GLM Coding Plan has no such flow, so its key is typed in instead — a static key rotates nothing and signs nothing out, which is what the CLI rule protects. Either way nothing is picked up from a CLI, and no credential belonging to one is ever read.
faq.a5: No. Softcap never reads or writes your CLI's credentials — it holds only the grants you gave it in the browser, and refreshing one touches nothing else on the machine.
faq.a6: In the macOS keychain, and nowhere else — never in preferences, logs or files. Removing an account removes its credentials from the keychain at that moment.
faq.a7: Three things, and only three: usage requests to your own providers, optional error reports scrubbed of paths and anything token-shaped, and an optional update check, daily and while its screen is open. The last two have their own off switches.
faq.a8: Those are the notification thresholds: a nudge when an account crosses 80% of a window, a last warning at 95% — once per crossing, not once per poll, and never during quiet hours. Both levels can be changed.
faq.a9: Every reading is taken at a moment and looked at afterwards. Softcap polls on a schedule, so the number on screen is as fresh as the last poll that landed — and when none has landed for a while, Softcap says how old the reading is instead of pretending it is live.
faq.lede: Short answers, each one true of the shipping app.

index.cell_alerts_h: It tells you before you hit it
index.cell_alerts_p:
At 80% and 95% out of the box, or whichever levels you set instead — once per
           crossing, not once per poll.
index.cell_keychain_p:
Credentials stay in the keychain, never copied into preferences or logs. When something
           fails, the app sends a description of the failure to its author, stripped of paths,
           addresses and anything token-shaped before it leaves the machine — and it can be
           switched off. The only other request is a check for a new version, daily and while the update screen is open, and that can
           be switched off too.
index.cell_langs_p:
Including Arabic, laid out right to left. Switching takes effect immediately, with no
           restart.
index.cell_quiet_p: Nothing arrives while you sleep, and nothing is delivered late to make up for it.
index.cell_timer_h: A timer in the menu bar
index.cell_timer_p:
The limit of the account you are working with, and how long until it frees up — without
           clicking. The strip can carry the countdown, the percentage, both, or just the icon,
           and a shortcut of your choosing opens the window without reaching for the mouse.
index.cell_widgets_p:
All four sizes on macOS. The same
           account row the window uses, so they cannot drift apart.

index.why_p1:
Softcap reads subscription usage directly for accounts added through the browser.
      These requests fetch limits without sending a prompt or running a model.
index.why_p2: Codex works the same way: sign in through the browser and Softcap reads that account's usage directly from the service. Nothing is taken from the CLI's own files, so what you see never depends on when Codex last ran.

limits.claude.counts_p: Prompts and the model work they cause count, scaled by model and length. Reading the usage endpoint does not: it is the same source the official clients consult, it carries no prompt, and it runs no model. Checking your limit does not spend your limit.
limits.claude.how_p1: A Claude subscription meters Claude Code through two windows at once. The session window opens with your first message and lasts five hours; the weekly window runs on its own seven-day cycle. Each has its own capacity, and hitting either one pauses the work until that window resets.
limits.claude.how_p2: The two windows are why usage feels confusing from inside a session: you can have plenty of week left and no session left, or the reverse, and the CLI only warns you when you are already close.
limits.claude.lede: The short version: two windows per account, refilling on their own schedules.
limits.claude.meta_description: The five-hour session window, the weekly cap, when each resets, what counts against them — and how to watch all of it without spending any of it.
limits.claude.og_description: The five-hour window, the weekly cap, and how to watch both without spending them.
limits.claude.other_pre: Running Codex too? Its limits behave differently:
limits.claude.reset_p: The session window resets five hours after it opened — not on the clock hour, and not at midnight. The weekly window resets on its own anchor, one moment in the week that is yours alone. Two accounts almost never share an anchor, which is exactly why a second plan helps: when one account is spent, the other is usually mid-refill.
limits.claude.title: Softcap — how Claude subscription limits work
limits.claude.watch_p: Softcap polls that endpoint with your own credentials and puts every account's two windows in the menu bar — with a countdown to the nearest reset, notifications at 80% and 95%, and widgets if you want them on the desk. Live readings, straight from the endpoint, for as many accounts as you have.
limits.codex.counts_p: Requests and the model work they cause count. Softcap's own usage requests do not send prompts and do not run models, so watching a limit never moves it.
limits.codex.how_p1: A Codex subscription meters use through a five-hour window and a weekly window, each with its own capacity. Hit either and Codex stops taking work on that account until the window resets.
limits.codex.how_p2: What makes Codex different is where the numbers live. The service reports what is left alongside its answers, and Softcap asks for those same figures directly, with a grant of its own — no prompt sent, no model run.
limits.codex.lede: The short version: the same two-window shape as Claude, read straight from the service.
limits.codex.meta_description: How OpenAI Codex meters subscription use — the five-hour and weekly windows, where the numbers come from, and how to watch them without spending them.
limits.codex.og_description: The five-hour and weekly windows, where the numbers come from, and how to watch them.
limits.codex.other_pre: Running Claude too? Its limits are metered live:
limits.codex.reset_p: The five-hour window rolls from your first request; the weekly window keeps its own anchor in the week, one per account. As with Claude, two accounts rarely reset together — the offset is the whole value of having both on one screen.
limits.codex.title: Softcap — how Codex rate limits work
limits.codex.watch_p: Sign a Codex account in through the browser and Softcap reads its usage live, with the reading's age shown honestly beside the number. Menu bar, thresholds at 80% and 95%, widgets.
privacy.changes_p: When this page changes, the date at the top changes with it. There is no mailing list to notify, because there are no addresses to mail.
privacy.children_p: Softcap is a developer tool, is not directed at children, and collects personal information from no one — children included.
privacy.contact_pre: Questions about any of this reach the author at
privacy.deletion_p: Removing an account inside Softcap removes its credentials from your keychain. Deleting the app removes the readings and their history — they existed nowhere else to begin with.
privacy.leaves_intro: Exactly three kinds of network traffic exist, and this is the complete list:
privacy.leaves_outro: There is nothing else. No telemetry, no crash-analytics service, no fingerprinting, no third-party SDK making calls of its own.
privacy.leaves_reports_d: when something fails, a description of the failure can be sent to the author. It is stripped of file paths, addresses and anything token-shaped before it leaves the machine, and the switch that turns it off is in Settings.
privacy.leaves_updates_d: once a day, and while the update screen is open, the copy from GitHub asks its release feed whether a newer version exists. That switch is in Settings too. The copy from the App Store asks nothing and has no update screen: the store looks after its own updates.
privacy.leaves_usage_d: the app asks Anthropic and OpenAI what is left of your subscriptions, using your own credentials. This is the app's function, and the requests carry no prompt and run no model.
privacy.meta_description: What Softcap stores, what leaves your Mac, and the two switches that turn the only optional traffic off. No accounts, no analytics, nothing sold.
privacy.og_description: No accounts, no analytics. Readings stay on the device; the only optional traffic has an off switch.
privacy.reports_p: An error report is a description of a failure: what broke, in which part of the app, on which app version and macOS version. The scrubber removes paths, host names, mail addresses and anything shaped like a credential before sending; reports go to the author's own collector at sentry.softcap.app and are used to fix the failure, then discarded.
privacy.short_p: Softcap has no user accounts, no analytics, and no advertising. It does not sell, share or monetise anything it handles. Your readings stay on your device.
privacy.stores_h: What the app stores, and where
privacy.stores_p1: Usage readings and their history live on your device. Credentials — the tokens that let the app ask a provider about your subscription — live in the system keychain, and are never copied into preferences, logs or files.
privacy.stores_p2: Softcap keeps no copy of any of this anywhere else. There is no server-side profile, because there is no server side.

support.a_keychain: That prompt is about Softcap's own container — the small file its widget reads — not about another app's data. macOS words it that way because these builds are signed ad-hoc rather than with a Developer ID, so it cannot confirm the app belongs to the team the container is filed under. Allow it and it stops asking until the next update. Decline and the menu bar and window work as usual; the widget and the statistics chart stay empty.
support.a_notify: Check three things: macOS notification permission for Softcap, the thresholds in Settings (80% and 95% out of the box), and quiet hours — nothing arrives while they are on, and nothing is delivered late to make up for it.
support.a_remove: Remove the account in Settings: its credentials leave your keychain at that moment. Nothing you signed into elsewhere is affected — Softcap holds only the grants you gave it.
support.a_reports: Both switches are in Settings. With them off, the only traffic the app makes is the usage requests to your own providers.
support.a_snapshot: Softcap polls on a schedule, so a reading is as fresh as the last poll that landed. Figures hours old mean the polls are not getting through — most often the account's grant has expired. Open Settings → Accounts: a row that needs attention says so, and Sign in… reconnects it.

terms.providers_p: Softcap reads your subscriptions with your own credentials, on your machine. Your Anthropic and OpenAI accounts remain governed by those companies' terms; Softcap neither extends nor circumvents them, and what you do with your accounts remains between you and your providers.

terms.title: Softcap — terms of use
terms.use_p: Use the app for what it is: a reader of your own subscription limits. Do not use it to misrepresent readings, to probe accounts that are not yours, or to abuse a provider's service.
terms.warranty_p: Softcap is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. A reading is a reading, not a guarantee — providers change their systems, and a number on screen can lag reality.
